svg.aria-label: The executable construction: hardware and software
svg.text: Native observer construction: finite hardware and two local laws
Hardware: twelve-port cells, seams, federations and registers. Software: two separate laws, supplied instruments, local protocol counts and retained records.
Declared preparations, local operations and comparisons produce
finite records. Agreement supports a shared interpretation.
The construction target includes an internal account of the
machine and its builders. The finite checks below establish
specified components; physical identification remains separate.

text.font-family: Menlo, Consolas, DejaVu Sans Mono, monospace

svg.text: An accepted unit move across a load difference of at least two
lowers Q = sum of squared loads by at least two. There are at
most Q(initial)/2 accepted moves. This depends on load size:
bounded loads give a polynomial bound in the port count;
arbitrary binary-encoded loads do not give a polynomial bound
in input length by this argument.
The coherent laws below have their own domains. This descent bound
does not supply a solver for general constraint problems.
One cell and federations of 20, 80 and 320 cells.
The arrays specify ports, seams and gluing.
The two laws act on different state spaces.
Their records require separate source maps.
A physical continuum limit is an additional claim.
the star of port 0: its five seams
a wedge: two seams at one port

svg.text: Each mode holds one object at most. An object on a seam moves through a wedge to the next seam of the same port.
The federation: cells on a sphere, one seam between neighbouring cells
Every dot is one whole cell of twelve ports. Every orange line is one external seam: it joins one port of a cell to one port of a neighbour.
A cell sits on a triangle of the sphere and has three neighbours. Each refinement cuts every triangle into four: 20, 80, 320 cells.
Filled dots: the three external ports of the cell lie symmetrically (pairwise two seams apart). Open dots: the gluing rule chose an unsymmetric triple.
Gluing rule of the builder (a declared convention): the external seam towards a neighbour leaves through the port whose direction, in the
local frame of the cell, points most nearly at that neighbour; two seams never share a port. A port therefore has five or six seams.
The spherical gluing is a declared carrier choice. A continuum conclusion requires a limit theorem for the chosen law and instruments.
The wiring between two cells of the 20-cell carrier
one external seam: port 3 of cell 0 to port 0 of cell 4
yellow ports carry the external seams of each cell; dotted stubs lead to the other neighbours

Complete cells with external port matching: P(pair; t) ≥ 1 − 40/(2κ − 6)²
for free evolution at every size and time. Finite emitters need their own error.

432 encoded bits; routed loop preparation adds twelve neutral scratch bits.
259 independent loop constraints select the sector of even total parity for 174 modes.
The displayed penalties are supplied code-protection terms; the accepted code is neutral.
The displayed levels are the spectrum of the declared free generator at m = 1.
Finite source-on pulses and approximate preparation determine the actual pointer laws.
Neutral scalar-code states do not establish a faithful charged response or an observed particle.
Round-sphere modifications change B and require their own source and instrument checks.

The diagram describes finite simulation-generated records. Preparation, scheduling, pulse strength and phase are supplied construction choices.
The source-energy ledger includes pulse driving work. It supplies neither controller energy accounting nor an autonomous clock or repeated reset budget.
Figures describe declared domains. Active contrast specification: model/polynomial_sv/SPEC.md. Scalar source map: model/np_scalar/PROOF.md.
